problem.statement: Build a distributed system on the assumption that remote calls between services always succeed (the network is reliable), omitting timeouts, retries, and failure handling.

approach.summary: Treat RPC/HTTP calls as if they were local in-process function calls that cannot fail or hang.

failure.point: Networks drop, delay, duplicate, reorder, and partition; calls that assume reliability hang on unbounded waits and cascade failures under real conditions.
failure.evidence: The "Fallacies of Distributed Computing" (Deutsch and Gosling; expanded by Rotem-Gal-Oz) list "the network is reliable" as the first fallacy; resilience guidance mandates timeouts, retries with backoff, and circuit breakers.

transferability.notes: Applies to all inter-process network communication. Genuinely in-process, single-node calls are exempt; more nodes and hops sharpen the failure.

confidence.notes: Codified industry principle; the failure manifests probabilistically under load and partitions rather than deterministically.
